candidates.why: Line 432 gets `name` from dwg_obj_table_get_name, which returns a malloc'd copy only when IS_FROM_TU_DWG(dwg) (dwg_api.c:20928-20931), otherwise a direct pointer to table->name. Line 437 frees it gated on IS_FROM_TU(dat) — a different macro. If the two disagree, line 437 frees a pointer that is still the live table->name field, so any later use of that field (e.g. next loop iteration / other writers) is a use-after-free. Also PAIR_S at 435 may skip printing when name is NULL while free still runs.

Line 461 gets `name` from dwg_ent_get_ltype_name, which returns the string literal "ByLayer" (dwg_api.c:20984) when no ltype, or a direct table->name pointer when not IS_FROM_TU_DWG. Line 466 frees it gated on IS_FROM_TU(dat). Freeing a literal or a non-owned field pointer is invalid; if it is the live ltype table->name, subsequent use is a UAF.

Line 574 sets pts = _obj->points (direct pointer into the object, not a copy). normalize_polygon_orient (582) may replace pts with a malloc'd copy (line 399) and return 1. Line 593 frees pts when changed. If normalize ever returns 1 without reassigning *pts_p (or on malloc failure at line 392 leaving new==NULL), pts still aliases _obj->points and line 593 frees the object's own points array, making later uses of _obj->points a UAF.

Line 710 orig=pts; normalize_polygon_orient (711) may set pts=new and return 1. Line 713 frees orig, then pts is used at 719-720 and freed at 724. If normalize returns 1 but leaves *pts_p unchanged (e.g. malloc failure at line 392 -> new==NULL, *pts_p=NULL), then pts==orig was already freed at 713 and line 719 dereferences freed/NULL pts — use-after-free.
